title: Morning Edition
dek: The AI buildout is colliding with the arithmetic of returns; a Thai island's sea turned green; research pushes the possible origin of animals deeper into time; and Maebashi is treating city-making itself as art.

lead_story.headline: AI's investment boom is running ahead of demonstrated productivity gains
lead_story.summary: Global data-center spending could exceed $30 trillion by 2050, while economists and industry studies say the productivity and revenue needed to justify today's AI buildout have not yet arrived at comparable scale.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The central AI question is shifting from whether the technology can do useful things to whether useful applications can generate enough economic value, soon enough, to support the infrastructure being built around them.

items.headline: A plankton bloom turned parts of the sea around Ko Lan bright green
items.summary: Heavy rain and flooding helped feed a Noctiluca plankton bloom around the Thai tourist island. Researchers are sampling the water while watching the larger concern: oxygen loss after blooms die off.
items.why_it_matters: The vivid surface color is temporary, but the underlying interaction among nutrient runoff, warmer water, flooding and hypoxia is a useful small-scale view of how coastal ecosystems can be stressed by several forces at once.

items.headline: A new analysis pushes the possible origin of animals hundreds of millions of years deeper
items.summary: Researchers argue that the absence of animals from exceptionally preserved ancient deposits cannot by itself establish that animals had not yet evolved, with modeling placing their possible origin around 800 to 700 million years ago.
items.why_it_matters: The result challenges a familiar inference from the fossil record and widens the poorly observed interval in which early animal evolution may have occurred.

items.headline: The Bank of England says AI-linked debt is becoming a financial-stability exposure
items.summary: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee said AI-related debt issuance has risen rapidly while broader geopolitical and energy shocks are also increasing stress in financial markets.
items.why_it_matters: AI is becoming not only a technology-sector story but a balance-sheet story: as more infrastructure is debt-financed, disappointment in demand or asset values can propagate through capital markets.

items.headline: Maebashi opened an art festival with carpenters raising a pillar to a traditional work chant
items.summary: The inaugural Maebashi Biennale in Gunma opened with local construction craftspeople performing kiyāri while lifting a pillar, tying contemporary art to the city's ongoing physical and cultural rebuilding.
items.why_it_matters: It is a small example of a city treating the people, trades and rituals that make a place as part of its cultural life rather than merely as background to it.

items.headline: Is intelligence more than optimization?
items.summary: Philosopher Sasha Mudd argues that defining intelligence only as successful optimization imports an engineering model into our picture of human reason, overlooking the capacity to examine and revise the ends we pursue.
items.why_it_matters: As machine systems become better optimizers, the argument forces a more precise question: whether intelligence means efficiently reaching a goal or also being able to judge which goals are worth having.

worth_your_time.headline: A Place Among the Fiddlers
worth_your_time.summary: At the Galax Old Fiddlers' Convention in southwest Virginia, thousands of musicians gather around an old-time and bluegrass tradition sustained as much in campsites and informal sessions as on the competition stage.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: The piece looks at how a living musical tradition survives: not as something preserved behind glass, but through repetition, apprenticeship, rivalry, friendship and people continuing to show up.
